description:
FILED s497b (the residue of #2103).  s497b enforces strict refs on every CAST (p-cast-@ / % / $ via :strict / :strict-lv) and on the element READS p-aref-deref / p-gethash-deref (:strict).  Not marked: the vivifying accessors p-ensure-hashref / p-ensure-arrayref / p-autoviv-* / p-viv-container (the write path and every intermediate level of a chain), p-funcall-ref (`&$str`, `$str->()`), and the glob deref p-dynamic-typeglob (`*{"..."}`).  Each lives where perl dies (the safe direction).

REPRODUCERS (perl 5.40.3 dies, PCL lives; each under `use strict`):
    my $s = "x"; $s->{k} = 1;
    my $h = {k => 1}; my $v = exists $h->{k}{j}{i};   # the fatals battery row "exists on non-element"
    my $s = "main::f"; &$s();
    *{"A::B"};
perl's t/lib/strict/refs cases 2, 4, 5, 21, 34, 37 (scratch/s497b/strict-refs-cases.pl).  Pl/t/fatals-01.t carries the exists row as a TODO naming this task.
SHAPE: the same site keyword on the vivifying family needs those forms to carry an optional site through p-setf's place tables and the autoviv macros (which today destructure with cadr/caddr and ignore extra args) -- measure the corpus-diff first.

=== RESIDUE (Fable review s499 of s497b's 91cfcfc0, appended by the s497b resume agent) ===
An RVALUE chain whose ROOT is an ELEMENT read is not marked.  Under `use strict`:
    my @a = (1); my $x = $a[0]->[0];      # perl: Can't use string ("1") as an ARRAY ref; PCL LIVES
    (same for a chain rooted at $h{k})
while `my $n = 5; $n->[0]` on a plain scalar DIES correctly.  So the miss is the `_deref_is_rvalue` whitelist (or the emitter) for a chain rooted at `$a[i]` / `$h{k}` rather than at a variable.  Reproducer: /home/bernt/pcl-agent-scratch/s499/review/q497-sigdie.pl row 15 (outputs under out/: perl -> rv-base -> rv-s497b).
subject: strict refs is NOT enforced on the WRITE / vivifying-chain path and for code/glob derefs: `$str->{k} = 1`, `push @{ $h->{l} }` over a string, `exists $h->{k}{j}{i}` through a non-ref, `&$str()`, `*{"name"}` live under `use strict` where perl dies
